notes: WebSearch reported the session-wide 200-call budget was already exhausted before this scout ran any query, so no WebSearch calls returned results (this is shared across all scouts in the sweep, not specific to this theme). DuckDuckGo html/lite endpoints returned CAPTCHA challenge pages to WebFetch every time. Bing search-results pages rendered to markdown by WebFetch's summarizer consistently omitted github.com links even when present in the raw HTML (the fetch tool's markdown conversion appears to drop or not follow through pagination/dynamic result blocks) - this looks like a WebFetch limitation worth flagging, not an absence of results. Fell back to `gh search repos` (4 allowed calls); 2 of the 4 hit GitHub's secondary rate limit (403) and were not retried per the 'up to 4 calls' cap, so a 5th call (cost of living index) was substituted instead of retrying the failed hotels.com/kayak queries. Net effect: this theme's coverage for Trivago/Hotels.com HPI archives and Kayak price trackers specifically is thin - I found no committed GitHub dataset or working client for any of Trivago tHPI (beyond one dead one-off 2015 analysis), Hotels.com HPI, Kayak price history, or Expatistan (zero hits of any kind for Expatistan on any method tried). Numbeo has a large population of scraper/API-client repos (all uncommitted-data, pull-on-demand methods against Numbeo's live pages) but essentially no repo commits a historical Numbeo dataset with dates attached - if the team wants Numbeo affordability data it will have to run one of these clients itself and stamp the pull date (per the point-in-time rule). Suggest a follow-up scout specifically on 'Big Mac index github', 'OECD PPP dataset github', or 'ECB effective exchange rate index github' as adjacent FX-affordability angles, and a second pass on Kayak/Hopper/Google Flights price-history repos using a plain browser (claude-in-chrome) rather than WebFetch, since WebFetch's markdown summarization seems to be silently dropping search-result links on both Bing and DuckDuckGo.

candidates.name: numbeopy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client (rate-limited, dependency-light) that pulls Numbeo's public cost-of-living pages via pandas.read_html: country-aggregate prices, per-city indices (50-70 price items per country incl. rent, restaurants, utilities, salaries), and country-level indices (6 cost-of-living sub-indices) plus category rankings (quality of life, property investment, crime, health care, pollution, traffic). No data committed; live pull only. CC BY-NC 4.0 license (non-commercial, attribution required, bulk redistribution discouraged). Last activity ~Jul 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Cleanest available Numbeo client for a repeatable, dateable pull of a global affordability/cost-of-living index across many cities - could be stamped and reused as a point-in-time consumer-affordability proxy (ties to gap #6, consumer spend panels) with minimal engineering; no committed history exists yet so it would need to be run and vintage-stamped by the team.
candidates.time_coverage: Live snapshot only, no historical data committed

candidates.name: numbeo-sql-importer
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Numbeo-org example repo showing how to import Numbeo's paid/official API cost-of-living data into SQL. Example/client code, not a dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms Numbeo has an official (paid) API path with structured city cost-of-living data; relevant if the team ever licenses Numbeo data directly rather than scraping.

candidates.name: numbeo_api_cost_of_living
candidates.what_it_holds: Scrapy-based scraper + Flask REST API + SQLite store for 12 cost-of-living indicators per city (meals, transport, utilities, internet, rent) scraped from Numbeo's public pages; JWT auth layer. No committed dataset, MIT license, 28 commits, marked 'under development'.
candidates.why_useful: Another reusable Numbeo scraper with a persistence layer already built (SQLite), which is closer to a repeatable point-in-time capture pipeline than a one-shot script.

candidates.name: scrape (numbeo cost-of-living scraper)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper pulling Numbeo cost-of-living components by country/location. Apache-2.0, 13 stars, updated Apr 2026. No committed CSV output in repo description.
candidates.why_useful: One more maintained Numbeo scraper option if the team wants to build its own point-in-time affordability panel.

candidates.name: trivago-Hotel-Price-Index-tHPI
candidates.what_it_holds: Small one-off data-science project analysing the Trivago Hotel Price Index (tHPI) for 2015; includes an R Markdown exploration file and an HTML demo. Scope/geography/exact data file unclear from the repo page (minimal README); appears to reuse a historical tHPI release rather than scraping live.
candidates.why_useful: Only repo found on GitHub that actually touches Trivago's Hotel Price Index (a real hotel-pricing benchmark series, analogous to what gap #8/#2 want for realized ADR/occupancy context); worth a closer look to see if the underlying 2015 tHPI figures are embedded in the Rmd, even though the index itself was discontinued and this is a single old snapshot.

candidates.name: hackpr-challenge (Puerto Rico COLI calculator)
candidates.what_it_holds: Hackathon challenge repo built around official Puerto Rico Institute of Statistics Cost-of-Living Index (COLI) data: 'COLI 2014Q3-2015Q3.xls' (quarterly index values, ~57 priced products, San Juan Metro vs ~300 C2ER regions) plus a 'Puerto Rico Index Compiler 2014Q3-2015Q3.xls' showing the aggregation formulas. Government-sourced, not crowdsourced, but a genuine point-in-time quarterly cost index with underlying category weights.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: shows how an official regional cost-of-living index (C2ER-style, same family as ACCRA/COLI that Numbeo/Expatistan approximate) is constructed quarter by quarter with full category weights - useful as a methodology reference for building a point-in-time affordability index, even though geography (Puerto Rico only) and vintage (2014-15) are narrow.
candidates.geography: Puerto Rico (San Juan Metro) vs ~300 US/Canada C2ER regions

candidates.name: city-cost-of-living-index (Kazakhstan)
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSVs (data/cost_piv.csv housing costs, data/spend_piv.csv monthly household expenditure) built from Kazakhstan's official stat.gov.kz economic-dynamics tables, plus a datapackage.json and processing scripts (cost.py, spend.py, datapack.py). Public-domain (ODC-PDDL) license. Government-sourced, not Numbeo/crowdsourced.
candidates.why_useful: A genuine committed cost-of-living dataset with a clear government source and reproducible build scripts, but narrow geography (Kazakhstan cities only) limits direct relevance to ABNB's core markets.
candidates.license: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication (ODC-PDDL)

candidates.name: india-cost-of-living-index
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed JSON dataset (public/data/cities.json) covering 50 Indian cities across 8 expense categories (housing, grocery, transport, healthcare, education, electricity, restaurant, movies), described as aggregated from 'multi-source data' (>50,000 data points), indexed to Delhi=100. Source methodology not fully documented in the visible README.
candidates.why_useful: A committed, structured cost-of-living panel for 50 Indian cities could be a useful India-specific affordability proxy for APAC regional splits (gap #7), though the undocumented sourcing and recency make it lower confidence than an official statistics series.
